raceHistory: 4 years recreational running before this plan
Mid-plan 5K time trial during Week 6 build
5K race: 24:51 on 2026-08-30 (goal was sub-25:00) — negative split, HR stayed below LTHR through km 4

currentForm.timeSincePeakFitness: 0 weeks — race just completed, this plan starts 1 week post-race

strengths.evidence: Disciplined pacing and negative-split execution on race day; cadence improved to 168-176spm; HR control shows real aerobic + threshold development from the last 10 weeks

limiters.evidence: Original limiter was inconsistent training frequency — resolved during the race build, but staying consistent with only 2-3 flexible sessions/week through a busier, colder, wetter season is the risk this plan is designed around

constraints: 2-3 runs/week capacity, no fixed days — work schedule varies week to week
Entering the cooler, wetter part of the year
No goal race currently scheduled — this is a maintenance, not a build, block
Racing a 4-mile turkey trot on 2026-11-26 (unplanned mid-block) — Week 12 restructured around it

hr.notes: Updated from LTHR ~165 to ~158, based on the Jul 31 time trial (25:47, avg HR 158, max 166) and the Aug 30 race (24:51, HR up to 166 sustained through km 5 at all-out effort). The original 165 estimate came from a single early training run and was consistently too high across every hard effort since.

pace.notes: Rebuilt around the diary's 5-tier system (E/M/T/I/R), anchored on Threshold pace — the most directly measured number, taken from the Jul 31 time trial run essentially at LTHR (158bpm) for 25+ minutes. Interval pace is validated by the actual VO2max session (4:47-5:04/km) and the race's middle kilometers (4:55/km). Recovery pace (6:15-6:45/km) sits below Easy and is used on cutback and post-race days. Easy pace is intentionally slower than recent training runs (5:36-6:00/km) — those were drifting toward Marathon-pace territory rather than true easy; the workouts below use true Easy pace. Pace-tier to HR-zone mapping, so the two tables stay in step: Threshold pace corresponds to HR zone 5a, Interval pace to 5b, Easy to zone 2, Recovery to zone 1-2.
pace.marathon: 5:20-5:30/km (speculative — no marathon-distance data yet; would need a long tempo effort or race to validate)

phases.name: Post-Race Reset
phases.focus: Clear race fatigue, then rebuild a normal three-run week
physiologicalGoals: Return to routine before any quality resumes

phases.name: Maintenance Cycle 1
phases.focus: Three load weeks then a cutback — the repeating four-week unit
keyWorkouts: One quality session per week (tempo and interval formats rotating)
Wednesday easy run paired with strength
physiologicalGoals: Hold LTHR and running economy near race-week levels
Keep enough top-end stimulus that VO2max doesn't decay

phases.name: Maintenance Cycle 2
phases.focus: Same four-week unit, different quality and long-run variants
keyWorkouts: One quality session per week (tempo and interval formats rotating)
Wednesday easy run paired with strength
physiologicalGoals: Sustain fitness through the darkest and wettest months
Vary the stimulus enough to avoid staleness

phases.name: Maintenance Cycle 3
phases.focus: Same unit again, with the turkey trot absorbed as week 13's hard session
keyWorkouts: 4-mile turkey trot as a low-key hard effort
Cutback and zone recalibration to close the block
physiologicalGoals: Carry fitness to the end of the block
Recalibrate zones off fresh race data

Flexible — move it to any day that works except Wednesday (your strength day), and ideally not the day straight after it. Keep at least one easy or rest day either side.

workouts.description: Same steady effort as the flat version, run on hills instead. Let the effort stay even — that means slowing on the climbs. workouts.description: Short and light — two days out from Thursday's race, the goal is to stay loose and sharp without adding any fatigue. This replaces the usual quality session this week. Kept on Tuesday deliberately rather than Monday: strides two days out is the right spacing.
workouts.humanReadable: 16min easy @ 5:55-6:20/km, then 4 x 100m relaxed strides @ ~5K effort with full recovery. Stop well short of tired.

workouts.name: Rest Day (light strength only)
workouts.description: Race is tomorrow — skip the usual paired run this week and go easy on the strength session too: keep loads moderate, skip anything maximal, and prioritize leaving the legs fresh over the session itself. If you can shift heavier lifting to earlier in the week just this once, that's even better.

workouts.name: 4-Mile Turkey Trot
workouts.description: Race day. Not a goal race — it's a low-key event that happens to fall inside this block, so it simply takes the place of the week's hard session. Run it for real, but don't build a taper around it. Based on your 24:51 5K (Aug 30), a fitness-equivalent 4-mile is roughly 32:00-33:00, i.e. 5:00-5:10/km (8:03-8:19/mi). Treat that as a guide, not a mandate — maintenance fitness sits a touch below race-peak, so run by feel (hard but controlled, 7-8/10). Same pacing discipline as your 5K: don't go out too hot in the first mile. Note that week 12 is a full load week with no cutback beforehand; that's intentional for a race at this priority.
workouts.humanReadable:
Warm-up: 12min easy jog + 4x100m strides
Race: 4mi (6.44km) @ ~5:00-5:10/km (8:03-8:19/mi), controlled start, hold through the middle, push if it's there in the last mile
Cool-down: 10min easy walk/jog
Duration and distance above include warm-up and cool-down; the race itself is ~32min.

Cutback weeks here trim volume by about 30%, not by half — at this mileage there is very little accumulated fatigue to shed, and cutting deeper just costs fitness. This is also the block's recalibration point: your Nov 26 race is fresh data, so re-derive LTHR and the pace tiers from it before starting the next cycle — the same way LTHR was corrected from 165 to 158 earlier this year. run.targetPace: n/a for the block — the only race is the Nov 26 turkey trot, paced 5:00-5:10/km in week 13
run.notes: There is no goal race in this block. One low-key race does fall inside it — the 4-mile turkey trot on 2026-11-26 — and it is handled as week 13's hard session rather than as a target: no taper into it, no cutback before it, and a recovery week after. Use the same pacing discipline as your sub-25 5K: slightly conservative first mile, even through the middle, push the last. If you later register an actual goal race, that needs a proper build rather than an adjustment to this block.

nutrition.preRace: Not applicable during maintenance — normal eating.
nutrition.notes: No race-day fueling needed for these sessions; just normal hydration, more so on longer steady runs in the heat... or, this time of year, layered up in the cold.

taper.notes: No taper in this block. The Nov 26 turkey trot gets a two-day easing-off (light Tuesday opener, no run and light lifting on Wednesday) rather than a real taper, which is appropriate for its priority. If you decide to target a goal race, tell me and I'll build a proper build/peak/taper plan from wherever your fitness is at that point.
